sanskrit: eṣa dhārayitā samyak cāturvarṇyaṃ mahābalaḥ śubhāśubham iva sphītā sarvasasyadharā dharā
english: This mighty one shall rightly uphold the four social orders, even as the earth — abundant and bearing all crops — sustains both the auspicious and the inauspicious.

sanskrit: asyājñāvaśagāḥ sarve bhaviṣyanti narādhipāḥ sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya vāyor iva śarīriṇaḥ
english: All kings shall come under his command, just as embodied beings are subject to the wind, which is the very self of all creatures.

sanskrit: eṣa rudraṃ mahādevaṃ tripurāntakaraṃ haram sarvalokeṣv atibalaḥ svayaṃ drakṣyati māgadhaḥ
english: This lord of Magadha, surpassing all in strength throughout the worlds, shall behold with his own eyes Rudra — the great god Hara, the destroyer of the triple city.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvann eva muniḥ svakāryārthaṃ vicintayan visarjayām āsa nṛpaṃ bṛhadratham athārihan
english: Speaking thus and reflecting upon his own purpose, the sage dismissed king Bṛhadratha, O slayer of foes.

sanskrit: praviśya nagaraṃ caiva jñātisaṃbandhibhir vṛtaḥ abhiṣicya jarāsaṃdhaṃ magadhādhipatis tadā bṛhadratho narapatiḥ parāṃ nirvṛtim āyayau
english: Returning to the city surrounded by kinsmen and relatives, the lord of Magadha, king Bṛhadratha, then consecrated Jarāsandha to the throne and attained supreme contentment.

sanskrit: abhiṣikte jarāsaṃdhe tadā rājā bṛhadrathaḥ patnīdvayenānugatas tapovanarato 'bhavat
english: Once Jarāsandha had been consecrated, king Bṛhadratha, accompanied by his two wives, devoted himself to the life of the forest-hermitage.

sanskrit: tapovanasthe pitari mātṛbhyāṃ saha bhārata jarāsaṃdhaḥ svavīryeṇa pārthivān akarod vaśe
english: While his father dwelt in the forest-hermitage together with his mothers, O Bhārata, Jarāsandha by his own valor brought the kings of the earth under his dominion.

sanskrit: atha dīrghasya kālasya tapovanagato nṛpaḥ sabhāryaḥ svargam agamat tapas taptvā bṛhadrathaḥ
english: Then, after a long time, king Bṛhadratha, dwelling in the hermitage and having practiced austerities, departed for heaven together with his wives.

sanskrit: tasyāstāṃ haṃsaḍibhakāv aśastranidhanāv ubhau mantre matimatāṃ śreṣṭhau yuddhaśāstraviśāradau
english: He had two ministers — Hamsa and Ḍibhaka — both of whom were destined to die without weapons, foremost among the wise in counsel, and skilled in the science of warfare.

sanskrit: yau tau mayā te kathitau pūrvam eva mahābalau trayas trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ paryāptā iti me matiḥ
english: Those two mighty ones of whom I spoke to you earlier — together with Jarāsandha, the three of them were, in my judgment, a match for the three worlds.

sanskrit: evam eṣa tadā vīra balibhiḥ kukurāndhakaiḥ vṛṣṇibhiś ca mahārāja nītihetor upekṣitaḥ
english: Thus was he, O hero and great king, left unchallenged at that time by the mighty Kukuras, Andhakas, and Vṛṣṇis — for reasons of statecraft.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca patitau haṃsaḍibhakau kaṃsāmātyau nipātitau jarāsaṃdhasya nidhane kālo 'yaṃ samupāgataḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: With Hamsa and Ḍibhaka — the ministers of Kaṃsa — slain and brought low, the time for Jarāsandha's destruction has now arrived.

sanskrit: na sa śakyo raṇe jetuṃ sarvair api surāsuraiḥ prāṇayuddhena jetavyaḥ sa ity upalabhāmahe
english: He cannot be conquered in open battle even by all the gods and demons together — we understand that he can only be overcome in a fight to the death, hand to hand.

sanskrit: mayi nītir balaṃ bhīme rakṣitā cāvayorjunaḥ sādhayiṣyāma taṃ rājan vayaṃ traya ivāgnayaḥ
english: In me resides policy; in Bhīma, strength; and Arjuna is the protector of us both. Together we shall accomplish this, O king — like the three sacred fires.

sanskrit: tribhir āsādito 'smābhir vijane sa narādhipaḥ na saṃdeho yathā yuddham ekenābhyupayāsyati
english: When that lord of men is confronted by three of us in a secluded place, there is no doubt he will accept to fight with only one of us.

sanskrit: avamānāc ca lokasya vyāyatatvāc ca dharṣitaḥ bhīmasenena yuddhāya dhruvam abhyupayāsyati
english: Stung by the contempt shown before the world and provoked by Bhīmasena, he will certainly come forward to fight.

sanskrit: alaṃ tasya mahābāhur bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ lokasya samudīrṇasya nidhanāyāntako yathā
english: The long-armed Bhīmasena of great strength is equal to destroying him — like Death come to end the life of one whose time has run out.

sanskrit: yadi te hṛdayaṃ vetti yadi te pratyayo mayi bhīmasenārjunau śīghraṃ nyāsabhūtau prayaccha me
english: If your heart knows this and if you have trust in me, then quickly entrust Bhīmasena and Arjuna to me as a sacred charge.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto bhagavatā pratyuvāca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmapārthau samālokya saṃprahṛṣṭamukhau sthitau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the blessed one, Yudhiṣṭhira replied, casting a glance at Bhīma and Pārtha who stood there with joyful faces.

sanskrit: acyutācyuta mā maivaṃ vyāharāmitrakarṣaṇa pāṇḍavānāṃ bhavān nātho bhavantaṃ cāśritā vayam
english: O Acyuta, O Acyuta — do not speak thus, O crusher of enemies! You are the lord and refuge of the Pāṇḍavas, and we take shelter in you.

sanskrit: yathā vadasi govinda sarvaṃ tad upapadyate na hi tvam agratas teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ lakṣmīḥ parāṅmukhī
english: Whatever you say, O Govinda, comes to pass — for fortune never turns her back on those who have you at their front.

sanskrit: nihataś ca jarāsaṃdho mokṣitāś ca mahīkṣitaḥ rājasūyaś ca me labdho nideśe tava tiṣṭhataḥ
english: Jarāsandha is as good as slain, the captive kings as good as freed, and the Rājasūya sacrifice as good as mine — for I stand under your direction.

sanskrit: kṣiprakārin yathā tv etat kāryaṃ samupapadyate mama kāryaṃ jagatkāryaṃ tathā kuru narottama
english: Act swiftly so that this task may be accomplished — my task which is also the task of the world. Do this, O best of men.

sanskrit: tribhir bhavadbhir hi vinā nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe dharmakāmārtharahito rogārta iva durgataḥ
english: Without the three of you I cannot bear to live — like one in misery who is afflicted by disease and bereft of dharma, desire, and wealth.

sanskrit: na śauriṇā vinā pārtho na śauriḥ pāṇḍavaṃ vinā nājeyo 'sty anayor loke kṛṣṇayor iti me matiḥ
english: Pārtha is nothing without Śauri, and Śauri nothing without the Pāṇḍava — in this world none can conquer either of the two Kṛṣṇas, so I believe.

sanskrit: ayaṃ ca balināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ śrīmān api vṛkodaraḥ yuvābhyāṃ sahito vīraḥ kiṃ na kuryān mahāyaśāḥ
english: And this glorious Vṛkodara, foremost among the strong, joined together with both of you — what could that illustrious hero not accomplish?

sanskrit: supraṇīto balaugho hi kurute kāryam uttamam andhaṃ jaḍaṃ balaṃ prāhuḥ praṇetavyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ
english: A mass of strength well directed accomplishes the highest deeds — raw strength without guidance is called blind and dull; it must be led by the wise.

sanskrit: yato hi nimnaṃ bhavati nayantīha tato jalam yataś chidraṃ tataś cāpi nayante dhīdhanā balam
english: Water flows wherever there is a downward slope; those rich in wisdom likewise direct an army wherever there is an opening.

sanskrit: tasmān nayavidhānajñaṃ puruṣaṃ lokaviśrutam vayam āśritya govindaṃ yatāmaḥ kāryasiddhaye
english: Therefore, taking refuge in Govinda — a man famed throughout the world and learned in the ways of statecraft — let us strive for the accomplishment of our purpose.

sanskrit: evaṃ prajñānayabalaṃ kriyopāyasamanvitam puraskurvīta kāryeṣu kṛṣṇa kāryārthasiddhaye
english: Thus one who combines wisdom, statecraft, and strength, and is furnished with the right means of action — place such a one, O Kṛṣṇa, in the forefront of all undertakings for the accomplishment of our aim.

sanskrit: evam eva yaduśreṣṭhaṃ pārthaḥ kāryārthasiddhaye arjunaḥ kṛṣṇam anvetu bhīmo 'nvetu dhanaṃjayam nayo jayo balaṃ caiva vikrame siddhim eṣyati
english: Even so, let Arjuna follow Kṛṣṇa, the foremost of the Yadus, for the accomplishment of the purpose, and let Bhīma follow Dhanañjaya — through policy, victory, and strength combined, success shall be attained in the campaign.

sanskrit: evam uktās tataḥ sarve bhrātaro vipulaujasaḥ vārṣṇeyaḥ pāṇḍaveyau ca pratasthur māgadhaṃ prati
english: Thus instructed, all those brothers of vast prowess — the scion of the Vṛṣṇis and the two Pāṇḍava heroes — then set out toward Magadha.

sanskrit: varcasvināṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ snātakānāṃ paricchadān ācchādya suhṛdāṃ vākyair manojñair abhinanditāḥ
english: Clad in the garments of radiant Brahmin graduates, they were bid farewell with affectionate and pleasing words by their friends.

sanskrit: amarṣād abhitaptānāṃ jñātyarthaṃ mukhyavāsasām ravisomāgnivapuṣāṃ bhīmam āsīt tadā vapuḥ
english: Wearing the chief garments of those who burn with indignation for the sake of their kinsmen — those whose forms blaze like the sun, moon, and fire — the appearance they presented then was awesome.

sanskrit: hataṃ mene jarāsaṃdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmapurogamau ekakāryasamudyuktau kṛṣṇau yuddhe 'parājitau
english: Seeing the two Kṛṣṇas — unconquered in battle, united in purpose, and with Bhīma leading the way — one would have reckoned Jarāsandha already slain.

sanskrit: īśau hi tau mahātmānau sarvakāryapravartane dharmārthakāmakāryāṇāṃ kāryāṇām iva nigrahe
english: For those two great-souled lords were capable of setting in motion any enterprise, just as they were capable of suppressing all matters pertaining to dharma, artha, and kama.

sanskrit: kurubhyaḥ prasthitās te tu madhyena kurujāṅgalam ramyaṃ padmasaro gatvā kālakūṭam atītya ca
english: Departing from the Kurus, they traveled through the heart of the Kurujāṅgala region, visiting the lovely Padmasara lake and passing beyond Kalakuta.

sanskrit: gaṇḍakīyāṃ tathā śoṇaṃ sadānīrāṃ tathaiva ca ekaparvatake nadyaḥ krameṇaitya vrajanti te
english: They crossed the Gandaki, then the Shona, then the Sadanira, and likewise the rivers near Ekaparvataka — proceeding onward one by one.

sanskrit: saṃtīrya sarayūṃ ramyāṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvāṃś ca kosalān atītya jagmur mithilāṃ mālāṃ carmaṇvatīṃ nadīm
english: Fording the lovely Sarayū and beholding the eastern Kosalas, they passed through Mithilā, and the river Mala, and the Carmaṇvatī.

sanskrit: uttīrya gaṅgāṃ śoṇaṃ ca sarve te prāṅmukhās trayaḥ kuravoraśchadaṃ jagmur māgadhaṃ kṣetram acyutāḥ
english: Having crossed the Gaṅgā and the Shona, all three of them — those unfailing heroes — proceeded eastward through the Kuraura forest into the territory of Magadha.

sanskrit: te śaśvad godhanākīrṇam ambumantaṃ śubhadrumam gorathaṃ girim āsādya dadṛśur māgadhaṃ puram
english: Reaching mount Goratha — ever filled with herds of cattle, rich with water, and adorned with beautiful trees — they beheld the city of Magadha.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca eṣa pārtha mahān svāduḥ paśumān nityam ambumān nirāmayaḥ suveśmāḍhyo niveśo māgadhaḥ śubhaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: O Pārtha, this Magadhan settlement is great, pleasant, ever well-stocked with cattle, rich in water, free from illness, furnished with fine dwellings, and auspicious.

sanskrit: vaihāro vipulaḥ śailo varāho vṛṣabhas tathā tathaivarṣigiris tāta śubhāś caityakapañcamāḥ
english: There is the great Vaihara mountain, and Varaha, and Vrishabha, and likewise Rishigiri, O dear one — and the auspicious Caityaka is the fifth of these.

sanskrit: ete pañca mahāśṛṅgāḥ parvatāḥ śītaladrumāḥ rakṣantīvābhisaṃhatya saṃhatāṅgā girivrajam
english: These five great-peaked mountains, shaded by cool trees, seem to stand united in body, guarding Girivraja together in a compact embrace.

sanskrit: puṣpaveṣṭitaśākhāgrair gandhavadbhir manoramaiḥ nigūḍhā iva lodhrāṇāṃ vanaiḥ kāmijanapriyaiḥ
english: With fragrant and charming trees whose branch-tips are wreathed with blossoms, the city lies concealed as if within the groves of lodhra trees so beloved by lovers.

sanskrit: śūdrāyāṃ gautamo yatra mahātmā saṃśitavrataḥ auśīnaryām ajanayat kākṣīvādīn sutān ṛṣiḥ
english: Here the great-souled sage Gautama, firm in his vows, fathered Kakṣīvat and other sons — upon a Śūdra woman and upon a woman of the Uśīnara clan.

sanskrit: gautamaḥ kṣayaṇād asmād athāsau tatra veśmani bhajate māgadhaṃ vaṃśaṃ sa nṛpāṇām anugrahāt
english: Gautama, descended from this lineage, still dwells in the hermitage there and is connected to the Magadhan royal line by the grace of its kings.

sanskrit: aṅgavaṅgādayaś caiva rājānaḥ sumahābalāḥ gautamakṣayam abhyetya ramante sma purārjuna
english: Kings of great strength — the rulers of Aṅga, Vaṅga, and others — used to come to Gautama's hermitage and take their pleasure there in former times, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: vanarājīs tu paśyemāḥ priyālānāṃ manoramāḥ lodhrāṇāṃ ca śubhāḥ pārtha gautamaukaḥsamīpajāḥ
english: Look at these rows of trees — the lovely priyala trees and the auspicious lodhra trees, O Pārtha — growing near the dwelling of Gautama.

sanskrit: arbudaḥ śakravāpī ca pannagau śatrutāpanau svastikasyālayaś cātra maṇināgasya cottamaḥ
english: Here are Arbuda and Shakravapi, two serpents who torment enemies; here too is the abode of Svastika, and the excellent dwelling of Maninaga.

sanskrit: aparihāryā meghānāṃ māgadheyaṃ maṇeḥ kṛte kauśiko maṇimāṃś caiva vavṛdhāte hy anugraham
english: The clouds cannot avoid shedding rain on the Magadhan land for the sake of this jewel-serpent; both Kauśika and Maninaga have grown in power by his favor.

sanskrit: arthasiddhiṃ tv anapagāṃ jarāsaṃdho 'bhimanyate vayam āsādane tasya darpam adya nihanma hi
english: Jarāsandha considers his prosperity to be unassailable — but today we shall strike down his pride by confronting him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tataḥ sarve bhrātaro vipulaujasaḥ vārṣṇeyaḥ pāṇḍaveyau ca pratasthur māgadhaṃ puram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, all those brothers of vast prowess — the scion of the Vṛṣṇis and the two Pāṇḍavas — then set out toward the city of Magadha.

sanskrit: tuṣṭapuṣṭajanopetaṃ cāturvarṇyajanākulam sphītotsavam anādhṛṣyam āseduś ca girivrajam
english: They reached Girivraja — filled with contented and well-fed people, crowded with the four social orders, abounding in festivals, and impregnable.

sanskrit: te 'tha dvāram anāsādya purasya girim ucchritam bārhadrathaiḥ pūjyamānaṃ tathā nagaravāsibhiḥ
english: Without approaching the gate, they made for the lofty mountain-range of the city — which was honored by the descendants of Bṛhadratha and by the city's inhabitants alike.

sanskrit: yatra māṣādam ṛṣabham āsasāda bṛhadrathaḥ taṃ hatvā māṣanālāś ca tisro bherīr akārayat
english: It was there that Bṛhadratha had encountered the bull that fed on beans; he slew it, had three great drums made from its hide and stalk-sinew,

sanskrit: ānahya carmaṇā tena sthāpayām āsa sve pure yatra tāḥ prāṇadan bheryo divyapuṣpāvacūrṇitāḥ
english: And, having covered them with its hide, installed them in his city — where those drums resounded, sprinkled with divine flowers.

sanskrit: māgadhānāṃ suruciraṃ caityakāntaṃ samādravan śirasīva jighāṃsanto jarāsaṃdhajighāṃsavaḥ
english: Those who sought to slay Jarāsandha rushed upon the lovely Caityaka peak of the Magadhans — as if intending to cut off a head.

sanskrit: sthiraṃ suvipulaṃ śṛṅgaṃ sumahāntaṃ purātanam arcitaṃ mālyadāmaiś ca satataṃ supratiṣṭhitam
english: It was a firm and very broad peak — vast and ancient, ever worshipped with garlands and wreaths, well established and revered.

sanskrit: vipulair bāhubhir vīrās te 'bhihatyābhyapātayan tatas te māgadhaṃ dṛṣṭvā puraṃ praviviśus tadā
english: The heroes shattered it with their powerful arms and brought it down; then, beholding the city of Magadha, they entered it.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu jarāsaṃdhaṃ samarcayan paryagni kurvaṃś ca nṛpaṃ dviradasthaṃ purohitāḥ
english: At that very moment the royal priests were performing rites of honor for Jarāsandha and leading the king, mounted on an elephant, around the sacred fire.

sanskrit: snātakavratinas te tu bāhuśastrā nirāyudhāḥ yuyutsavaḥ praviviśur jarāsaṃdhena bhārata
english: Those three, observing the vows of Brahmin graduates — with their arms as their only weapons, bearing no other armament, and eager to fight — entered together with Jarāsandha, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: bhakṣyamālyāpaṇānāṃ ca dadṛśuḥ śriyam uttamām sphītāṃ sarvaguṇopetāṃ sarvakāmasamṛddhinīm
english: They beheld the supreme splendor of the food-stalls and flower-shops — prosperous, endowed with every good quality, and abounding in all desirable things.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā samṛddhiṃ te vīthyāṃ tasyāṃ narottamāḥ rājamārgeṇa gacchantaḥ kṛṣṇabhīmadhanaṃjayāḥ
english: Seeing this prosperity, those foremost of men — Kṛṣṇa, Bhīma, and Dhanañjaya — proceeded along the royal road through that market-lane.

sanskrit: balād gṛhītvā mālyāni mālākārān mahābalāḥ virāgavasanāḥ sarve sragviṇo mṛṣṭakuṇḍalāḥ
english: Those mighty men forcibly took garlands from the garland-sellers; all of them clad in faded garments, wearing flower-wreaths and gleaming earrings.

sanskrit: niveśanam athājagmur jarāsaṃdhasya dhīmataḥ govāsam iva vīkṣantaḥ siṃhā haimavatā yathā
english: They then approached the dwelling of the wise Jarāsandha, gazing about as if surveying a cow-pasture — like lions from the Himālayan slopes.

sanskrit: śailastambhanibhās teṣāṃ candanāgurubhūṣitāḥ aśobhanta mahārāja bāhavo bāhuśālinām
english: Their arms — anointed with sandal and aloe-wood, resembling stone pillars — shone brilliantly, O great king, those arms of those mighty-armed heroes.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā dviradaprakhyāñ śālaskandhān ivodgatān vyūḍhoraskān māgadhānāṃ vismayaḥ samajāyata
english: Seeing them — broad-chested, resembling elephants, rising like the trunks of sala trees — amazement arose among the Magadhans.

sanskrit: te tv atītya janākīrṇās tisraḥ kakṣyā nararṣabhāḥ ahaṃkāreṇa rājānam upatasthur mahābalāḥ
english: Those foremost of men, of great strength, passed through three crowd-filled outer enclosures and then approached the king with self-assurance.

sanskrit: tān pādyamadhuparkārhān mānārhān satkṛtiṃ gatān pratyutthāya jarāsaṃdha upatasthe yathāvidhi
english: Jarāsandha rose to receive them — for they were worthy of the water-offering and the honey-gift, worthy of honor, and deserving of respectful welcome — and attended to them according to the prescribed rites.

sanskrit: uvāca caitān rājāsau svāgataṃ vo 'stv iti prabhuḥ tasya hy etad vrataṃ rājan babhūva bhuvi viśrutam
english: That lord and king said to them: "Welcome to you all." For this was a vow of his, O king — widely renowned throughout the earth.

sanskrit: snātakān brāhmaṇān prāptāñ śrutvā sa samitiṃjayaḥ apy ardharātre nṛpatiḥ pratyudgacchati bhārata
english: Even at midnight, O Bhārata, that conqueror of assemblies — that king — would go forth to receive Brahmin graduates who had arrived.

sanskrit: tāṃs tv apūrveṇa veṣeṇa dṛṣṭvā nṛpatisattamaḥ upatasthe jarāsaṃdho vismitaś cābhavat tadā
english: But seeing them in their unusual attire, the foremost of kings — Jarāsandha — attended to them and was filled with wonder.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvaiva rājānaṃ jarāsaṃdhaṃ nararṣabhāḥ idam ūcur amitraghnāḥ sarve bharatasattama
english: But those foremost of men — slayers of enemies all — upon seeing king Jarāsandha, spoke thus, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: svasty astu kuśalaṃ rājann iti sarve vyavasthitāḥ taṃ nṛpaṃ nṛpaśārdūla vipraikṣanta parasparam
english: "May it go well with you, O king — be in good health" — so they all said as they stood there; then, O tiger among kings, they gazed at each other and at that king.

sanskrit: tān abravīj jarāsaṃdhas tadā yādavapāṇḍavān āsyatām iti rājendra brāhmaṇacchadmasaṃvṛtān
english: Then Jarāsandha addressed those Yādavas and Pāṇḍavas — concealed beneath the disguise of Brahmins — saying: "Be seated, O lords."

sanskrit: athopaviviśuḥ sarve trayas te puruṣarṣabhāḥ saṃpradīptās trayo lakṣmyā mahādhvara ivāgnayaḥ
english: Then all three of those foremost of men took their seats — blazing with splendor, the three of them like the three sacred fires at a great sacrifice.

sanskrit: tān uvāca jarāsaṃdhaḥ satyasaṃdho narādhipaḥ vigarhamāṇaḥ kauravya veṣagrahaṇakāraṇāt
english: Then Jarāsandha — that truthful lord of men — addressed them, reproaching them on account of the reason for their disguise, O Kauravya.

sanskrit: na snātakavratā viprā bahirmālyānulepanāḥ bhavantīti nṛloke 'smin viditaṃ mama sarvaśaḥ
english: "It is known to me in every way, in this world of men, that Brahmins who observe the vows of graduates do not wear their garlands and unguents on the outside of their garments."

sanskrit: te yūyaṃ puṣpavantaś ca bhujair jyāghātalakṣaṇaiḥ bibhrataḥ kṣātram ojaś ca brāhmaṇyaṃ pratijānatha
english: "Yet you wear flowers, and you bear the marks of bowstrings on your arms — you carry the energy of the warrior class, yet you claim to be Brahmins."
